name: The Abbasid translation movement at the House of Wisdom
summary: Caliph al-Maʾmūn institutionalises the systematic translation of Greek philosophical, mathematical, medical, and astronomical texts into Arabic at Baghdad. Translators (Hunayn ibn Ishaq, Thabit ibn Qurra) work from Greek and Syriac sources; original research follows (Khwārizmī's algebra, Khwārizmī's astronomical tables).

_quarry.structural_significance: Preserves most surviving classical Greek scientific writing, particularly Aristotle, Euclid, Ptolemy, Galen, and dramatically advances it. The Arabic corpus becomes the basis of the 12th-13th-century Latin translation movement (Toledo, Sicily) that drives the rise of European universities.
